builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MINE: Entropy-coded Memory-efficient Inference for Large Language Models
summary: MINE replaces standard quantized-weight storage and dequantization kernels in single-stream inference with a lossless entropy coding scheme (dtANS-LLM) that compresses the non-uniform weight distribution and integrates into vLLM as a plugin. It costs per-tensor and per-GPU auto-tuning of compression hyper-parameters, adds entropy-decoding compute to each weight fetch, and demonstrated results depend on a specific EntQuant checkpoint format rather than arbitrary quantized models. Adoption can fail if the reader's models lack compatible checkpoints, if decode overhead erases the compression gain on different GPUs, or if the workload batches requests, since the benefit targets strictly single-stream, memory-bound decoding.
rationale: The reader's 24 GB GPU profile matches the paper's single-stream local-inference setting, but the gain is hardware- and checkpoint-specific and requires validation on the reader's own models and GPU before production use.
technique: Entropy-coded weight compression for memory-bound decoding

It costs per-tensor and per-GPU auto-tuning of compression hyper-parameters, adds entropy-decoding compute to each weight fetch, and demonstrated results depend on a specific EntQuant checkpoint format rather than arbitrary quantized models. Adoption can fail if the reader's models lack compatible checkpoints, if decode overhead erases the compression gain on different GPUs, or if the workload batches requests, since the benefit targets strictly single-stream, memory-bound decoding.
2.52x and 1.48x speedups over the fastest baseline on RTX 4060 Ti and RTX 5090 with a 2.1-bit EntQuant Llama 3.1 8B checkpoint, at 2.24 and 3.43 effective bits per weight.
